q: 1. Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2026?
explain: Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her contribution to bringing those involved in war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide within the scope of the law, and to strengthening international law.

q: 2. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2026?
options: Francis Halzen (Belgium/USA) and Henri B. Kagan (France)
Karl Deisseroth (USA), Peter Hegemann (Germany) and Georg Nagel (Germany)
Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (USA)
explain: Karl Deisseroth (USA), Peter Hegemann (Germany) and Georg Nagel (Germany) received the Nobel Prize in Medicine for their important discoveries on light-driven ion channels and optogenetics.

q: 3. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2026?
explain: Francis Halzen was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contribution to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos.

q: 4. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2026?
options: Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan)
Robert E. Hall (USA) and Karl Deisseroth (USA)
explain: Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan) were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their discoveries on a special type of chemical process in the creation of organic substances and on spontaneous (auto-)catalysis.

q: 5. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2026?
explain: Anne Carson (Canada) was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for creating a new dimension and form in contemporary literature through a living dialogue with classical tradition.

q: 6. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2026?
options: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (USA)
Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan)
explain: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (both USA) were awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics for their contribution to strengthening macroeconomic stability.

q: 7. When and where was the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) held?
explain: Nepal was represented at the Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania by Speaker Dip Prasad Aryal. Nepal had tabled the Bhotekoshi flood issue as an emergency proposal, and it secured more than the required two-thirds of votes.

q: 8. When is World Post Day observed?
explain: The day is observed because the Universal Postal Union (UPU) was established on 9 October 1874. The 2026 (152nd) theme: 'One Postal Network, Infinite Possibilities'. Nepal obtained membership on 11 October 1956 (B.S. 2013 Asoj 26).

q: 9. When did the famous Indian actor Nana (Vishwanath) Patekar pass away?
explain: Nana Patekar was born on 1 January 1951 in Maharashtra. His first film was 'Gaman' (1979). He received the Padma Shri honour in 2013.

q: 10. When did the devastating flood occur in the Budhigandaki River?
explain: The sudden flood occurred when a dam burst after a massive landslide in Chumnubri Rural Municipality, Gorkha, blocked the river. Four dozen houses were completely destroyed, and three permanent (pucca) bridges and three suspension bridges were damaged.

q: 11. Who is the thinker who said, 'For happiness, there must be harmony in your thoughts, words and deeds'?
explain: This thought is attributed to Mahatma Gandhi.

q: 12. How many national languages has the Koshi Province Government recognized as languages of government work?
explain: Besides Nepali, Koshi Province has recognized 13 national languages: Maithili, Limbu, Tharu, Tamang, Magar, Bantawa, Urdu, Rajbanshi, Rai, Newar, Chamling, Sherpa and Santhali.

q: 13. When was Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) established?
explain: APEC was established in 1989. Its headquarters is in Singapore, and its first meeting was held in Australia in 1989.

q: 14. Until when was the practice of writing the tithi and weekday while mentioning dates in documents in Nepal in force?
explain: The practice of writing the tithi and weekday in documents remained in force until B.S. 1961 Magh.

q: 15. Making a major achievement in the field of communication technology, which country has recently put into operation the world's first 'Pre-6G' test network?
explain: China has launched the world's first 'Pre-6G' test network, which has 10 times more capacity than the currently used 5G. Its features include high bandwidth, minimum delay (low latency) and easy integration of artificial intelligence. Test areas: holographic communication, robotics and embedded intelligence, industrial manufacturing, and low-altitude inspection.

q: 16. What is the 'Jitugi' concept related to?
explain: The 'Jitugi' concept is related to foreign employment.

q: 17. When did Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle make the Economic Status Paper 2083 public?
explain: Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle made the Economic Status Paper 2083 public on B.S. 2083 Baisakh 14.

q: 18. What is the process of transferring an employee from one place to another, or assigning responsibility, on the basis of qualification, capability, performance, experience and skill called?
explain: It was started in Nepal by the new government from B.S. 2082 Chaitra. Appointments or transfers are made purely on the basis of performance and qualification, not on political pressure, access, personal relations or favoritism.

q: 19. According to Nepal's current Economic Status Paper 2083, what percentage is the contribution of the agriculture sector to Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
explain: Agriculture contributes 25.2 percent to GDP. The service sector's contribution rose from 57.5 percent to 62 percent, while industry's fell from 14.1 percent to 12.8 percent. Remittances contribute 27.5 percent.

q: 20. Which bank was honored as the 'Best Managed Commercial Bank of the Year 2026' at the 10th 'Newbiz Conclave and Business Excellence Awards 2026'?
explain: Everest Bank was honored as the 'Best Managed Commercial Bank of the Year 2026' at the 10th Newbiz Conclave and Business Excellence Awards 2026.
